title: Tensorized KV cache reconstruction with Mirror role views
hypothesis: A shared K/V cache tensor plus per-layer/head Mirror coordinates can reconstruct aligned KV role states using fewer bytes than full or generic Tucker/PCA state, while preserving attention context; independent role states reveal the private-cache boundary.
physical_object: shared key and value base cache tensors of shape [32,16] for 16 layer/head roles
mirror_coordinate: one Givens angle per role for K and V
logical_multiplicity: 8 layers × 2 KV heads = 16 role-specific cache tensors
controls: MLKV-style one shared K/V state broadcast to every role
Mirror shared cache bases plus role angles

development.selection_metric: actual bytes, cache NRMSE, attention context NRMSE, decode/materialization time

storage.authority: actual serialized fp16 inference payload bytes
paid_objects: independent K/V tensors or shared K/V bases and role angles/factors
storage.runtime_cache: all 16 role tensors × 32 tokens × 16 dims are represented by each method's payload

success_gate: Aligned attention context NRMSE <=0.05 and at least 20% fewer bytes than generic Tucker/PCA; decode cost and cache bandwidth must be reported. Independent roles test private cache need.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality/storage gate or generic PCA matches/improves the frontier; independent role caches requiring full state are a boundary result.

compute.report_materialization_macs: estimated MACs for cached K/V role materialization; zero for full stored state and broadcast MLKV

boundaries: Deterministic random queries, no autoregressive generation
Aligned teacher generated by same Givens rotations
No end-to-end decode throughput or language perplexity
